what: Draft: whom each domain declares as its partners, up to 3 in and 3 out (frame/links.ts Partners). A draft for the evaluation to come; not wired into the city yet (the city's districts are still the Console's menu).
why: The Owner, 2026-11-20: the rules first; detect before judging. The named ports are the partners a domain declares; traffic with anyone undeclared goes to Other. This draft is read from what exists, so the gap between it and what each domain says it wants is the first thing to judge.
drafted_by: the city line (cockpit), 2026-11-20, for the Owner; each domain's line confirms or changes its own row
direction: in: others come to it (they call its API or tool, or it receives their event); out: it goes to others (it publishes an event they receive, or calls theirs). The town has no outside (the Owner, 2026-11-20: it is the whole system), so every user is a domain inside it.

foundation.note: Used by every kind of caller; its 65 contracts are mostly the unclaimed default bucket (network, telemetry, alerts, bus, MCP), not the foundation itself.

lineage.note: Three callers in (the console, the agents' tools, Trade); its main-advanced event goes out to delivery and verification.

verification.note: Trade (tenant) also reads it: undeclared, so Other in.

delivery.note: Five want in (lineage, verification, owner, coordination, tenant): two go to Other. The most connected domain.

approvals.note: The console is itself. Research (tenant) asks it questions.

compute.note: Its alerts go to coordination's alert letters; MCP reads it.

payload.note: Its users are its own satellites (Trade, Research, plugins): inside it, a black box each. Seven callers on one module.

coordination.note: Receives compute's alerts and the seats' mail; the console reads it.

gaps: Direct references from one domain's code into another's insides are not measured yet (CLAUDE.md §1, 2026-11-16); this draft sees only declared contracts and the bus.
Who reads whose metrics is not declared anywhere yet; the metric way has no rows here.
Commands (MCP tools, actions) carry no consumers in the ownership table, so they are not counted.
Where the console and the agents' tools belong (owner, coordination) is a proposal; if they are a domain of their own, the rows change.

users_inside.why: The Owner, 2026-11-20: the town is the whole system; Trade, Finance and the other payloads are inside it, each a satellite of the tenant domain, a black box to us that opens onto its own world. So the callers the ownership table names are mapped to the domain they belong to. PROPOSED: each line confirms.
users_inside.console: owner (the Owner's console: his decisions and his view)
users_inside.mcp: coordination (the agents' tool counter: the seats)
users_inside.trade-infra, trade-api, trade-frontend,: tenant (the payloads and the plugins; each tenant a satellite, a black box)
